claims.title: Attack the edit distance barrier via Galois-style invariant obstruction
claims.statement: Instead of searching for subquadratic algorithms or refining reductions, identify an invariant that any strongly subquadratic edit-distance algorithm would have to preserve (a coarse-graining under which alignment information collapses), and show the invariant is absent. Impossibility becomes structural, mirroring Galois's treatment of the quintic.
claims.source: cross-domain combination of breakthrough:galois with problem:edit-distance-barrier

axis_texts.semantic: Prove the quadratic barrier structurally: find what every fast algorithm must respect and show it is missing.
axis_texts.mechanism: shift from algorithm search to invariant structure any successful method must respect; obstruction becomes provable
axis_texts.math_structure: invariant theory fine-grained reductions information content of dynamic programming tables
axis_texts.problem_shape: formula search replaced by structural obstruction
axis_texts.failure: edit distance may lack a group-like structure; invariants may be too weak or vacuous

metadata.bridge: Galois's move: replace 'try harder to solve' with 'characterize what any solution preserves'. For algorithms: characterize what any subquadratic comparison can read.
metadata.cheap_falsification: Attempt the invariant formalization on a toy variant (e.g., bounded-alphabet LCS); if even there no nontrivial invariant separates fast from slow algorithms within a month of effort, downgrade.

verification.summary: 136 exact-DP pairs probed: every cheap statistic is either provably foolable on structured families or reduces to known statements; the pre-registered AGAINST bar was not fully met. A live Galois route would need a sketch that provably bounds what any o(n^2)-time algorithm extracts.

claims.title: Intermittency as typicality: ensemble counting of extreme vorticity configurations
claims.statement: Rather than deriving intermittency from cascade dynamics, treat anomalous exponents as a counting question: enumerate (via large-deviation/ensemble methods) which velocity-field configurations dominate high-order structure functions, and derive the multifractal spectrum as the entropy of that configuration ensemble.
claims.source: cross-domain combination of breakthrough:boltzmann-statistical with problem:turbulence-intermittency

axis_texts.semantic: Reframe intermittency from dynamical derivation to counting which extreme configurations are typical at each order.
axis_texts.mechanism: reframe deterministic question as ensemble counting; moments dominated by configuration classes weighted by their entropy-like weight
axis_texts.math_structure: large deviations ensemble counting multifractals saddle-point asymptotics
axis_texts.problem_shape: derivation replaced by classification + counting of dominant configurations
axis_texts.failure: configuration space may be uncountable in useful coordinates; weights may be dynamics-dependent, reintroducing the unsolved problem

metadata.bridge: Boltzmann's move: give up trajectory-level explanation; define the right ensemble and count. Extreme events become 'rare but numerous' classes.
metadata.cheap_falsification: On shell-resolved DNS data or shell models, test whether a two-parameter configuration-entropy fit reproduces known intermittency exponents p=1..8 better than log-Poisson cascades; if not competitive, discard.

verification.summary: Sabra shell model (N=22) zeta_p p=1..8: bimodal entropy ensemble fails outright (single-kink spectrum, RMS ~0.30); best parabolic rate-function variant merely matches parameter-free She-Leveque (0.025 vs 0.031 RMS) and is an order of magnitude worse than log-Poisson at equal fitting freedom while reducing to log-normal phenomenology - counting adds nothing beyond cascade encoding. The hypothesis's anticipated failure mode (weights are dynamics-dependent) confirmed.

claims.title: Kohn-Sham-style surrogate twin for enzyme catalysis decomposition
claims.statement: Replace the contested decomposition of enzyme rate acceleration with a fictitious solvable reference reaction constrained to match observables (rate constant, isotope effects) exactly; concentrate all model error into one exchange-like functional term. The attribution debate becomes the study of that single functional's variation across enzymes.
claims.source: cross-domain combination of breakthrough:kohn-sham with problem:enzyme-catalysis-origin

axis_texts.semantic: Stop partitioning the free-energy surface; build a solvable twin reaction matching observables and push all ambiguity into one improvable functional.
axis_texts.mechanism: surrogate system matches target observable-by-observable; error concentrated in single improvable component
axis_texts.math_structure: variational reference systems functional decomposition self-consistent calibration
axis_texts.problem_shape: attribution problem converted into functional approximation problem
axis_texts.failure: no choice of reference reaction may make the residual term small enough across enzyme families

metadata.bridge: Kohn-Sham's move: exactness relocated into a black box improved indefinitely, surrogate stays solvable. Attribution disputes become functional design.
metadata.cheap_falsification: Take one enzyme family with mutational rate data; fit the surrogate-twin functional to half the mutants and predict the rest. Prediction error above Arrhenius-fit baselines kills it.

claims.title: Glassy arrest as self-templated configurational order (prion pattern)
claims.statement: Hypothesize that below the glass transition the amorphous configuration itself acts as its own template: local structural order propagates by templated conversion of neighbors without any thermodynamic singularity or external carrier. The thermodynamic-versus-kinetic dichotomy is then malformed - the carrier of 'order' is the configuration history itself, analogous to prions carrying form without genome.
claims.source: cross-domain combination of breakthrough:prion with problem:glass-transition

axis_texts.semantic: Ask whether glassy order propagates like a prion: the arrangement templates itself, dissolving the transition-vs-crossover dichotomy.
axis_texts.mechanism: separate informational process (templated propagation of local order) from assumed carrier (thermodynamic phase)
axis_texts.math_structure: nucleation templated growth kinetic arrest cooperative relaxation dynamic heterogeneity
axis_texts.problem_shape: false-dichotomy dissolution by redefining the carrier of order
axis_texts.failure: tempered glass phenomenology may be fully explained by existing RFOT/MCT; templating adds nothing falsifiable

metadata.bridge: Prion's move: strip the process to its abstract transfer rule, find minimal carrier. Here the candidate carrier is the configuration itself.
metadata.cheap_falsification: Colloidal glasses: check whether locally-ordered regions grow by boundary conversion kinetics (templated) versus bulk nucleation; distinguishable growth-law exponent.

verification.summary: 2D spin-flip KCM (FA facilitation, exact detailed balance), L=126, quench to T=1.5: growth-kinetics discrimination between templated/interface-limited, nucleation, and coarsening channels was INCONCLUSIVE under pre-registered criteria (amendments v2/v2.1 registered before fits; two inadmissible batches archived).

claims.title: Forcing-style world construction for planted clique thresholds
claims.statement: Treat the planted-clique threshold like Cohen treated set-theoretic independence: explicitly engineer random-graph worlds realizing each candidate answer (detectable at k, undetectable at k) via generic constructions whose properties are controlled through finite approximation, aiming to show threshold location is a property of the construction method, not of nature.
claims.source: cross-domain combination of breakthrough:cohen-forcing with problem:planted-clique-hardness

axis_texts.semantic: Build explicit worlds where the planted clique is easy/hard at the same k, forcing the conclusion that 'hardness' is method-relative and constructively manipulable.
axis_texts.mechanism: engineer environments realizing each outcome; truth value becomes design parameter controlled by finite approximations
axis_texts.math_structure: generic constructions conditional distributions indistinguishability sum-of-squares worlds
axis_texts.problem_shape: prove separation by constructing both universes rather than bounding one
axis_texts.failure: indistinguishability between engineered worlds may collapse to known pseudodistribution bounds; nothing beyond SSE lower limits

metadata.bridge: Cohen's move: if undecided inside, build larger universes realizing each outcome. For average-case complexity: build input ensembles making each behavior actual.
metadata.cheap_falsification: Try engineering two k ~ log^2(n) ensembles that are statistically close yet separate a specific algorithm class (e.g., SDP-based); if closeness always forces same SDP outcome, the constructive program stalls early.

verification.summary: Pre-registered forcing-style construction at n=1000: engineered worlds matched on chosen statistics but zero implemented detectors (greedy, spectral, combinatorial) separated them - AGAINST per pre-registration. Scale-limited; recorded as evidence the constructive program needs larger n or stronger statistics.

claims.title: Prior-free auctions by hedging: make unknown value distributions cancel
claims.statement: Import Black-Scholes-Merton's replication logic into auction design: construct payment/allocation mechanisms as portfolios over simple auction instruments such that dependence on the unknown bidder-value distribution cancels by construction, yielding prior-free guarantees the way delta-hedging yields preference-free prices.
claims.source: cross-domain combination of breakthrough:black-scholes with problem:auction-design-robustness

axis_texts.semantic: Do not estimate bidder values; design the mechanism so distributional uncertainty cancels dynamically, as hedging cancels risk premia.
axis_texts.mechanism: dynamic composite mechanism makes unknown parameter cancel; guarantees by construction not estimation
axis_texts.math_structure: replication portfolios worst-case competitive ratios online learning duality minimax
axis_texts.problem_shape: unknown environment made harmless by constructed strategy
axis_texts.failure: auction allocation discreteness may block continuous rebalancing analogues; cancellation may need clairvoyance

metadata.bridge: Black-Scholes's move: stop predicting the underlying; build output from hedge. Auctions: stop learning the distribution; build revenue from offsetting positions across bidders/types.
metadata.cheap_falsification: Single-item case: does a dynamic portfolio of posted prices replicate the optimal-distribution benchmark within constant factor without samples? If even this fails, combinatorial version hopeless.

verification.summary: Sample-free dynamic posted-price portfolios (exp3, exp3-anytime, uniform-mix) achieve CR mean <10 and worst-seed <50 vs clairvoyant fixed-price benchmark across all test families (uniform, power-law, bimodal, adversarial permutations). Pre-registered SUPPORT criteria met; advances with stricter criteria.

claims.title: Loop invariants as Noether conserved quantities of transition symmetries
claims.statement: Treat loop invariants as conserved quantities generated by symmetries of the loop's transition relation: identify transformation groups under which the transition system is invariant, and derive invariants as Noether-type currents instead of searching template space. Inference becomes symmetry detection.
claims.source: cross-domain combination of breakthrough:noether with problem:loop-invariant-inference

axis_texts.semantic: Derive loop invariants from symmetries of the transition relation instead of searching for them.
axis_texts.mechanism: vary execution under transformation groups preserving transitions; boundary terms yield conserved assertion forms
axis_texts.math_structure: group actions on state space fixed points polynomial ideals inductive assertions
axis_texts.problem_shape: search problem converted into structure-detection problem
axis_texts.failure: most practical loops have only trivial symmetries; generated currents may be weaker than needed invariants

metadata.bridge: Noether's move: conservation is derived from invariance. Programs: assertions preserved by all executions should be derived from transformations preserving the transition relation.
metadata.cheap_falsification: Benchmark suite (e.g., SV-COMP loops): detect automorphism-like symmetries of integer transition relations; measure how often symmetry-derived candidates match the verification-grade invariant. Below ~20% coverage, pattern too thin.

verification.summary: 30 SV-COMP-style integer loops, exact rational polynomial engine. Extended coverage 23/30=76.7%, strict (finite automorphisms only) 15/30=50.0% - both clear the 20% kill bar, including nonlinear invariants (y-x^2) found as eigenforms of mixed-rate scaling symmetries. Misses: quadratic conserved quantities with no point symmetry, non-polynomial/gcd targets, irrational-eigenvalue (golden ratio) symmetries, inequality-only control-heavy loops.
verification.caveat: translation-duality half of extended coverage reduces to constant-shift linear-invariant generation; honest reading is pure symmetry detection carries ~half the benchmark

stage2.summary: Real SV-COMP corpus vs linear template baseline under pre-registered rules: baseline-symmetry gap 15.15pt misses the 15pt UPGRADE window by 0.15; nonlinear wins 7 (>=5); DOWNGRADE conditions not met. Post-hoc: strict-symmetry gap equals exactly the translation-duality share; quadratic-accumulator loops need cohomological-equation solving beyond point symmetries.

claims.title: Anesthesia mechanism via Bethe-ansatz consistency across agents
claims.statement: Postulate a restricted circuit-level form for consciousness disruption (e.g., a factorized interaction between arousal nuclei and cortical inhibition), then require consistency across pharmacologically diverse anesthetics. As in the Bethe ansatz, cross-agent consistency conditions may quantize the possible mechanisms to a small discrete set, converting a many-to-one mystery into constraint solving.
claims.source: cross-domain combination of breakthrough:bethe-ansatz with problem:anesthesia-mechanism

axis_texts.semantic: Assume the mechanism's circuit form first; demand consistency across chemically diverse agents; let constraints select the mechanism.
axis_texts.mechanism: ansatz-first restricted solution shape; consistency around diverse perturbations yields exact restrictions
axis_texts.math_structure: factorized interactions consistency conditions constraint satisfaction network dynamics
axis_texts.problem_shape: many-to-one convergence reduced to consistency-filtered hypothesis set
axis_texts.failure: anesthetic diversity may act through genuinely non-factorizable pathways; consistency conditions may be satisfied trivially

metadata.bridge: Bethe's move: write down the solution's form before the derivation; internal consistency does the proving. Diverse anesthetics play the role of particle exchanges around which consistency is demanded.
metadata.cheap_falsification: Fit the factorized circuit ansatz to published EEG dose-response data for 3+ agent classes; if no common reduced parameterization fits within reasonable error, the ansatz class is wrong.

claims.title: Union-closed abundance as a typicality statement
claims.statement: Strip Frankl's conjecture of set-theoretic meaning and keep only statistics: model union closure as a channel merging information sources, and ask whether the abundant element is forced by a Shannon-style typicality/capacity argument. Conjecture: union closure implies an entropy inequality whose consequence is the >=1/2 frequency bound.
claims.source: cross-domain combination of breakthrough:shannon-entropy with problem:frankl-union-closed

axis_texts.semantic: Read union closure as an information-merging operation; prove element abundance as a statistical necessity.
axis_texts.mechanism: discard structure retain frequencies; closure as noisy channel; abundance as capacity/typicality phenomenon
axis_texts.math_structure: entropy inequalities set systems shearer's inequality extremal frequency bounds
axis_texts.problem_shape: combinatorial existence converted into information inequality
axis_texts.failure: known entropy approaches (Shearer-based) already stalled; channel view may add nothing

metadata.bridge: Shannon's move: strip meaning, keep statistics. Union-closed families: forget what sets mean; frequencies under a merge operation obey information inequalities.
metadata.cheap_falsification: Search for a union-closed family violating the proposed entropy inequality computationally up to ground size ~30; a counterexample to the inequality route appears quickly if it exists.

verification.summary: Exhaustive n=4 + 59k samples n=6-8: naive entropy ceilings (I2), one-bit-merge Shearer bound (I3), dropout monotonicity (I5) are violated by real union-closed families; surviving bounds (Reimer, Knill) provably do not imply Frankl, and the distribution-universal ceiling saturates exactly at t=1/2 so no ceiling-type inequality can cross the Frankl boundary. Controls show entropy stats barely distinguish closed from unclosed families.

claims.title: Sex as active maintenance of Mendelian discreteness
claims.statement: Invert Mendel's move: his breakthrough discretized heredity against blending appearance; recombination's evolutionary role can be framed as the machinery actively defending that discreteness against informational decay. Hypothesis: sex is selected as error-correction for the discrete substrate - recombination restores integer-like genotypes degraded by mutation and drift, paying the twofold cost when degradation rates exceed a threshold expressible in mutation-rate units.
claims.source: cross-domain combination of breakthrough:mendel with problem:evolution-of-sex

axis_texts.semantic: Frame recombination as defense of hereditary discreteness; sex pays off exactly when discrete units degrade faster than selection repairs them.
axis_texts.mechanism: discretize hidden substrate; identify process that maintains discreteness; derive cost-benefit threshold from degradation rate
axis_texts.math_structure: mutation-selection balance linkage disequilibrium information decay error-correcting codes
axis_texts.problem_shape: many competing benefits reduced to single threshold criterion testable by rate measurements
axis_texts.failure: mutation-rate threshold predictions may sit far from observed biological regimes; classic mutational-deterministic critique applies

metadata.bridge: Mendel's move reversed onto its own domain: discreteness was the insight; ask what maintains it. Sex = maintenance protocol for the discrete substrate.
metadata.cheap_falsification: Cross-species comparison: correlate recombination rates with measured genomic degradation proxies (mutation rate x genome length, transposable load). Predicted positive threshold-like relation either holds in existing datasets or does not.
